Ondas has transformed its revenue profile through strategic m&a, expanded its markets, & positioned itself to compete for larger, more complex defense programs. But what would your alternative strategy have been, & how would it have delivered comparable commercial scale without raising capital?

items.title: @UwUSenpai I am certainly growingly concerned that this $NVDA scandal is a giant accounting scandal and violation of law scandal with export
items.content_excerpt: @UwUSenpai I am certainly growingly concerned that this $NVDA scandal is a giant accounting scandal and violation of law scandal with export controls. I have never, for a second, believed it had anything to do with sex. You don’t dismantle someone as big as Jensen and as indispensable as Jensen to the entire industry and to one of the biggest companies in the world over poor judgment about sex partners where it was consensual. I am a lot more worried about violation of export control laws and other potential accounting irregularities other practices to ensure that $NVDA always met or exceeded the Wall Street expectations for earnings. Which it did religiously. I’ve always known that Jensen would do almost anything to meet the numbers. Including, for example, selling just the number of chips that needed to be sold to $CRWV to meet numbers that I’ve seen, because I used to be a big shareholder in CoreWeave and follow their finances closely. Thankfully, $APLD is really not very dependent on $NVDA for anything. $NVDA divested itself of $APLD stock in favor of Neocloud stock, and there’s no circular financing between APLD and Nvidia that’s ever been disclosed or known. However, $CRWV, which is closely financially intertwined with Nvidia, including Nvidia backstopping all of its unused capacity as well as NVDA owning about 10% of its shares, is a tenant constituting $11 billion of the $36 billion in APLD contractual backlog. The good news is $META is the compute client at the CoreWeave data center (Polaris Forge 1), and I have a feeling that if $CRWV were to fall on its face, $META would probably want to take the site over as the tenant to continue the compute servicing. No guarantees on that, but that’s a really, really strong tenant to have there, and they’re not going want that ready compute capacity to go away at a time when there is an incredible shortage of compute capacity and data centers to service it. Still, I think it’s more likely than not we’re in the hunt for some rough sledding the next few weeks with this $NBIS scandal developing. The onion of that scandal has yet to be peeled back. We just don’t know the full extent of what was done. We’re not done. To me, $NVDA stock is uninvestable, at least for me. It’s certainly not going to go to zero, but it could take a giant hit IF there was large-scale misconduct.

items.title: $APLD has two concrete milestones next week: a Louisiana project vote on November 19 and a federal permitting-bill vote on November 16. Loui
items.content_excerpt: $APLD has two concrete milestones next week: a Louisiana project vote on November 19 and a federal permitting-bill vote on November 16. Louisiana is the more direct company-specific catalyst. Both could affect sentiment and reduce uncertainty, but neither should be confused with completed financing or final passage of legislation. Thursday, November 19, at 5 p.m. ET: England Authority’s draft agenda lists a vote authorizing the PILOT (payment in lieu of taxes) lease AND bond agreement with APLD AEX-01 LLC. The proposed framework covers 300 MW of critical IT load and permits up to $4.6 billion in bond issuance, subject to conditions. Approval would advance the local tax-incentive and financing framework. However it does not mean $4.6 billion has been raised. Bond buyers, financing terms, State Bond Commission approval and actual issuance remain separate hurdles. messages.body: $VSTM $RVMD Patient fitness remains one of the most precious and rapidly depleting resources in PDAC. The availability of increasingly effective therapies does not eliminate line-to-line attrition. The attrition curve deserves attention alongside the survival curve.
